articles.title: ‘Those Are the Wrong Reasons to Make a Movie’ — Godzilla Minus Zero Director Takashi Yamazaki on Setting Aside the Urge to One-Up Godzilla Minus One
articles.summary: Godzilla Minus Zero writer, director, and VFX supervisor Takashi Yamazaki says that getting caught up in besting Godzilla Minus One "risked diluting what makes the movie great in the first place."
articles.body:
How does a filmmaker attempt to follow up a history-making movie with an even bigger and better sequel? For Godzilla Minus One and Zero writer, director, and VFX supervisor Takashi Yamazaki, that line of thinking doesn’t even belong in the equation.

“In the beginning I thought, ‘Well, how do I outdo its predecessor and how do we make a movie that's going to win all these awards and it's going to be bigger in scale?’” Yamazaki told IGN during an interview near Godzilla Minus Zero’s debut at the New York Film Festival. “But I think it's very dangerous to create a movie with that type of mindset because you're going to risk diluting what makes the movie great in the first place. So those are the wrong reasons to make a movie and it ends up becoming an antagonist in your moviemaking process.”

Godzilla Minus One was released in 2023 and quickly caught fire. Yamazaki’s take on a post-WWII Godzilla was especially praised for its human-focused story and highly impressive VFX, done with a famously lean team of 35 artists . It went on to beat Hideaki Anno’s 2016 Shin Godzilla at the box office, becoming the highest-grossing Godzilla movie to date . At the 2024 Oscars, where the cast and crew walked the red carpet holding Godzilla figurines and wearing very cool Godzilla shoes, the film took home the trophy for Best Visual Effects.

The win was historic on many levels: It was the first Japanese film to claim the award, minted the first Gen Z winner in the category , and did so with the smallest budget of any other category in more than a decade . (Reports had put the cost between $10–15 million.)

“Godzilla Minus One was loved and so well received by so many around the world and received a lot of awards, which I think was unthinkable when we first set out and went to make it,” Yamazaki said. “So thinking about a sequel, of course, there's gonna be a certain amount of pressure.”

Godzilla Minus Zero is due out in the U.S. this week — it opened in Japan on November 3 for Godzilla Day — and the anticipation is high following its film festival premieres this fall that have been universally rapturous. Naturally, it’s a bigger film in just about every way. First and foremost, it’s got an extra kaiju (which means, a new pair of shoes to go with it). It’s both the first R-rated Godzilla movie and the first Japanese film to be specifically shot for IMAX screens.

At a panel at New York Comic-Con, the aforementioned Gen Z Oscar winner, VFX artist and compositor Tatsuji Nojima, gave an example of just how much more intensive the effects process becomes with that extra screen space: The shot of Godzilla leaping out of the ocean behind a seaplane from the first trailer was made entirely using VFX that required rendering 2 billion particles, versus the 200 million particles needed for an ocean sequence in Godzilla Minus One. (Nojima also shared that the scene was made by just two people: himself and an animator.) Though the exact figures are unknown, Yamazaki has confirmed that the budget was certainly bigger this time around. It’s projected to rake in $25–35 million its opening weekend, according to Box Office Pro , which would more than double Godzilla Minus One’s first weekend earnings of $11.4 million.

Still, for Yamazaki, the important part of making a successful sequel was in rejecting the anxiety of feeling like he needed to one-up Godzilla Minus One at all.

“I think when I decided not to think about it was a huge sense of relief for me and just simply focus on making a movie entertaining, making something fun, making something that has a message,” he said. “The moment where I felt like, yes, I did it was probably when I shed off all that extra pressure and thought, ‘You know what? I'm just going to make a fun movie.’ [That] was my own tipping point.”

Godzilla Minus Zero opens in the U.S. on Friday, November 6. We said it “ups the ante on the carnage, providing plenty of satisfying and visually amazing scenes of giant-monster destruction” in our review .

articles.title: Blackpink's Jisoo Confirms She Referenced Resident Evil's Ada Wong in New Music Video
articles.summary: Blackpink’s Jisoo has confirmed that she referenced Resident Evil’s Ada Wong in the music video for her solo song Addicted.
articles.body:
Blackpink’s Jisoo has confirmed that she referenced Resident Evil’s Ada Wong in the music video for her solo song, Addicted.

The song debuted over Halloween weekend, with its accompanying music video showing Jisoo wearing a variety of different looks. One of these outfits, however, struck a chord with certain members of her fanbase due to how startlingly similar it looked to a character from Resident Evil .

At the beginning of the music video, Jisoo wears a black bob and a red bodycon-style dress — a look that’s basically synonymous with Ada Wong, who almost always wears some variation of this style in each game she appears in.

Fans couldn’t help but notice the similarities and asked the K-pop star if this was intentional on her very own app. “Red outfit + short hair look is totally Ada Wong from Resident Evil,” one wrote.

Surprisingly, Jisoo confirmed that this was actually intentional. "I love Biohazard (Resident Evil) sooo much, so I wanted to copy it,” she said in a reply.

Jisoo is open about her love for Resident Evil; she spoke about the series on Hot Ones earlier this year, saying she was “addicted” to the games.

“It’s fast-paced,” she explained. “Something will suddenly pop out at you, so you have to be quick and process it all and take care of the situation. That’s why it’s able to hold my attention, and time just flies right by.”

Funnily enough, Jisoo isn’t the only K-pop star to draw comparisons with Ada Wong recently; in August, Babymonster’s Asa received similar comments from fans after she posted photos of herself on social media wearing a black bob and a red dress , sparking a cute portmanteau of ‘Asa Wong’ from her fanbase.

While Asa hasn’t yet responded to these remarks, Jisoo is an unabashed fan of the games, to the point where she made sure Ada was somehow represented in her latest song.

In other Resident Evil news, Zach Cregger, who directed the series’ most recent movie adaptation, said he would still like to be involved in some way if a sequel gets made, though not as a director. Thus far, it’s unclear whether or not another Resi movie is in the works, but given that Capcom has doubled down on its plans to continue expanding its IP with merch, new content, and movies, it’s possible that we get another look at Raccoon City — especially given how successful the first film was at the box office .

articles.title: Terminally Ill GTA 6 Fan Dies 3 Weeks Before Game's Launch, Fans Pay Their Respects
articles.summary: A terminally ill GTA 6 fan has died three weeks before the game's launch.
articles.body:
A terminally ill GTA 6 fan has died three weeks before the game's launch.

Back in August, a man named Jerry, known online as Void Only, made a viral TikTok video revealing that he had been hospitalized due to an interstitial lung disease and was in need of a lung transplant. However, he noted that his unique situation meant that his lungs were attached to his chest wall, and any surgery would be bloody and dangerous. In that same post, he noted that he just wanted to play GTA 6, and poked fun at Rockstar's many delays for the game. In the comments, fellow players rallied around him and were rooting for him to keep going until the release of GTA 6.

A GoFundMe was set up to pay for his transplant and other needs, with supporters donating $50,000 in a matter of days . In September, Jerry got his transplant, but various complications eventually caused him to lose function of his body. Jerry's sister confirmed via his socials that he died over the weekend, but was extremely appreciative of all of the people who tried to help and support him. The news comes just three weeks before GTA 6's release, which Jerry had planned to stream with his community once it was released.

In the comments of his sister's post, fans expressed sadness over Jerry not being able to make it to the release of the game he'd been excitedly waiting so long to play.

"I was really rooting for him. I'm sorry for your loss," said one commenter.

"I'm adding Void to my gamertag in his honor when GTA releases," said another.

This tragic outcome has left supporters devastated. Jerry himself stayed optimistic in his final months and kept a positive attitude, prompting fans to echo his enthusiasm. Jerry's sister also noted that his mother is planning to do a balloon release in his honor, and more details will be shared at a later date.

articles.title: Project Hail Mary Author Andy Weir Explains How He Would Fix the Star Wars Franchise
articles.summary: Andy Weir, famous for penning The Martian and Project Hail Mary, has some strong ideas about how he would tackle telling stories in the Star Wars universe if he had the chance.
articles.body:
Andy Weir, famous for penning The Martian and Project Hail Mary , has some strong ideas about how he would tackle telling stories in the Star Wars universe if he had the chance.

Andy Weir is well-versed in writing sci-fi stories with mass appeal. He is the author of two major novels in the genre, after all, both of which have been given the Hollywood treatment with big-budget film adaptations. And while his own tales have captivated audiences for over a decade, he has a good idea of what he’d do if he got put in charge of some pre-existing source material.

In a November 2 interview with SlashFilm , Weirs was asked what he’d do if he were in charge of the Star Wars franchise — and he had a decisive answer. According to Weirs, moving away from the Galactic Civil War isn’t something that most fans are likely to get excited about; thus, in his opinion, a return to that time period focusing on different characters is the way to go.

We Build Star Wars Executor Super Star Destroyer

"Star Wars is more about massive upheaval. One problem that happens is, if you're going to have a story about a monumental war, then when it's over and the good guys win, you want it to stay that way. So it's very unsatisfying if you roll into a new monumental war,” he began.

“I feel like the best way, in my opinion, to do another Star Wars movie — and I'm not George Lucas and this might be a terrible idea — would be to have the story of other people during the Galactic Civil War.

“Think of it like this: We know what happened in World War II, but there are some really good fictional stories that take place during World War II. So if you treat the Galactic Civil War as, 'Okay, that's established canon, those are the things that happened,' but there's still a lot of stories to tell about other people living through those wars. So that's what I would do."

To this point, Weirs had nothing but praise for Andor, Disney’s Star Wars series that takes place just before the Galactic Civil war with a focus on several different characters and their roles in the rebellion. However, he doesn’t feel like its sprawling story is something that could be translated to the big screen for a two-hour viewing experience.

"Andor was amazing and really good, and it was a series and [that was the correct choice]. You're going to do a movie, you've got to tell your whole story in like two hours. So it needs to have a lot more — 'Andor' was very intellectual, extremely clever, extraordinarily well-written, very well — I mean, I loved everything about it. But it's not something that you could make into a movie,” he said.

This is the latest big news to come from Weirs following his comments on AI , which are pretty bleak. Also speaking with SlashFilm, Weir admitted that it’s “only a matter of time” before the technology proliferates in careers like his, saying he “might be among the last generation of fully human writers."

articles.title: The Rings of Power Season 3 Co-Showrunner Confirms Harfoots Will Return
articles.summary: Contrary to earlier reports, the Harfoots are still a part of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, Season 3 albeit not to the degree they were featured in the Prime Video show’s first two seasons.
articles.body:
Contrary to earlier reports , the Harfoots are still a part of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power , Season 3 albeit not to the degree they were featured in the Prime Video show’s first two seasons.

“[We] have not written out the Harfoots [from Season 3]”, co-showrunner Patrick McKay recently informed me at the show’s press junket.

“I would say for myself and J.D. [Payne], my co-show runner, every season is its own opportunity and its own challenge. With Season 3, we really wanted to level up our game as dramatists. We really wanted to focus the show. We wanted to be more psychological, more emotional, wanted to do a darker season,” McKay explained.

“It's the season where Sauron forges the One Ring , and we wanted that to unify every single storyline. We didn't want it to have sprawl the way we enjoyed having in the past. No, no. This was a time we wanted it to be one journey and on rails.”

McKay continued: “That meant that if a story wasn't about the rings and wasn't about Sauron and wasn't about the One Ring, that to put it in there would feel forced and it wouldn't do justice to those characters. But don't worry, you can't count a halfling out, the Harfoots and Markella [Kavenagh] and Megan [Richardson]'s characters. They'll be back maybe sooner than you think.”

How exactly the Harfoots will factor into the overall plot to stop Sauron from forging the One Ring – and just how much they will actually appear in Season 3 – remains to be seen.

The last time we saw the Harfoots at the end of Season 2 , Nori Brandyfoot (Kavenagh) and her bestie Poppy Proudfellow (Richardson) bid farewell to the Stranger (Daniel Weyman). The two duo joined the Stoors as they left looking to find a new home after the Dark Wizard (Ciaran Hinds) destroyed their canyon. By the end of the Season 2 finale , the Stranger is dubbed “Grand Elf” by the Stoors, and thus the name Gandalf is born.

The Rings of Power, Season 3 picks the story up five years later and chronicles the war to stop Sauron from forging the One Ring and binding its peoples to his will. The season introduces new characters, including an enigmatic “Orc with an Arc” who may or may not be an ally to the Elves.

The first four episodes of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, Season 3 will premiere on November 11, 2026. Episodes 305 & 306 will be available to stream on November 18, while the final two episodes of the season will be released on November 25.

articles.title: Johnny Depp Is Open to Playing Jack Sparrow Again in a New Pirates of the Caribbean Movie
articles.summary: Johnny Depp is open to playing Jack Sparrow again in a new Pirates of the Caribbean movie, despite saying he'd never work with Disney on the franchise ever again.
articles.body:
Johnny Depp is open to playing Jack Sparrow again in a new Pirates of the Caribbean movie, despite saying he'd never work with Disney on the franchise ever again.

In a recent interview with Entertainment Tonight , Depp was asked if he had any interest in playing Sparrow again. He noted that he wanted to send the franchise off on a better note, presumably referring to the last film being a critical disappointment.

"If things are exactly where they need to be with regard to how they're going to top off the Pirates [story]. The only involvement I really want to have, truly, is just to send them off on a better note. I'll go to work with [Jerry] Bruckheimer tomorrow for anything. If it's Jerry, I trust him. We have a deep friendship."

Depp had previously stated during his legal battle with Amber Heard that he wouldn't work with Disney on a new Pirates movie , not even for $300 million and a million alpaca. It seems he's softened his stance on the matter, which has reportedly been the case for a while. Producer Jerry Bruckheimer has stated a few times over the last couple of years that he was having conversations with Depp about a new Pirates movie , but nothing has been locked in place. There is, however, a screenplay in the works , and the producer hopes to get a deal signed with Depp.

This is the first time Depp has publicly revealed he's open to the idea since swearing off the idea in 2023. Disney had also been exploring a new Pirates of the Caribbean movie with Margot Robbie in the lead role, but that has yet to make any kind of notable progress. Depp hasn't been in many blockbuster roles since his legal battle with Heard, and he was notably forced to step down from his role in the Fantastic Beasts films due to his libel case against UK outlet The Sun. He was replaced by actor Mads Mikkelsen for the third film in the franchise, which also happened to be the last.

Deep is now set to star in a new take on A Christmas Carol with the film Ebenezer , which releases on November 13. Whether Jack Sparrow will set sail again remains to be seen, but he does appear to be more into the idea than he was before.

articles.title: John Goodman Says Digger Reviews 'Killed' the Movie Before It Was Released
articles.summary: John Goodman believes the critical reception to Digger "killed" the movie before it had even been released.
articles.body:
John Goodman believes the critical reception to Digger "killed" the movie before it had even been released.

Tom Cruise's latest film, Digger, is one of the biggest Hollywood bombs of 2026 . So far, the film has only made $49 million on a reported budget between $125–180 million, meaning it won't come close to breaking even in its theatrical run and probably won't make up the difference on home video. Given Cruise is seen as one of the last true movie stars, it was a pretty devastating blow.

Cruise's Digger co-star, John Goodman, spoke about the situation with Josh Horowitz and believed that critics pushed anyone away from seeing it. Digger's Rotten Tomatoes score sits at 53%, making it one of Cruise's most divisive movies and the lowest-rated film in his filmography since 2017's The Mummy.

"It hurt. They kinda killed us before we opened [with headlines like], 'This will only make $5," said Goodman. "And it [felt like] a good reason for people to avoid it. I'm proud of it. I had a ball doing it."

Goodman went on to state that he believed in the message of Digger and defended the film, despite it not being universally loved. IGN gave Digger a 6 out of 10 , noting that the movie lacks the bite needed to sell its message, but has great performances and humor.

"Digger's satire may not change your thinking on global warming, but there are excellent performances and more than a few laughs," reads an excerpt from our review. "If you're an AMC A-List member (or have another cinema subscription), Digger is worth catching on the big screen."

Maybe Digger will be one of those movies that ages well and fans will feel was misjudged. However, it may be years before it gets any kind of meaningful reevaluation. Whether this will deter Cruise from doing more big swings also remains to be seen, but at least the team behind the film stands by it.

articles.title: A Concerning Amount of GTA Fans Would Give Up Their Pets to Play GTA 6 Early
articles.summary: A poll of 1,300 American gamers shows some concerning trends regarding GTA 6 — more specifically, their willingness to abandon their pets for a chance at playing the game ahead of its release.
articles.body:
A poll of 1,300 American gamers shows some concerning trends regarding GTA 6 — more specifically, their willingness to abandon their pets for a chance at playing the game ahead of its release.

GTA 6 might be the biggest pop culture phenomenon in human history. It’s certainly one of the most expensive video games ever made with a marketing budget to match, considering that Rockstar has literally taken over Miami with oodles of Vice City branding, alongside a collaboration with the Miami Heat .

Before GTA 6’s big debut on Netflix , fans were literally camping outside of Rockstar’s headquarters, using special equipment to monitor oxygen levels , sound volume, and even count cars going in and out of the building for just a sliver of information about the highly-anticipated title.

With just a few more weeks until launch, fans are more amped than ever to play the game — and some would even give up pretty important things if they had the chance to experience it before everyone else.

A new survey by Unwind Media polled 1,347 American gamers to see how they felt about GTA 6. And while there were more than a few surprising responses, one stood out from the rest; according to the survey, 7% of polled fans said they would literally give up their pet for a month if they got to play the game a week early.

Out of these fans, those who already pre-ordered the game were more likely to give up certain things. The number of deadbeat pet parents doubled within this group, with 13% of players who pre-ordered GTA 6 saying they would be willing to give up their pet to play it early.

Other surprising admissions from the survey found that 21% of all fans polled would willingly give up intimacy to play GTA 6 a week early, meaning that one in five fans would make the trade. Of those fans, 25% were female, as opposed to 19% of male players.

However, more heartwarmingly, over half of all participants said they planned to play the game together with their partner. A whopping 53% of those polled answered that this would be a good activity to play with their partner in crime; and funnily enough, more women than men were keen on doing this. 71% of gals are absolutely down to rob virtual corner stores with their boo, compared to 39% of dudes.

This is good news, especially after a trend swept across social media that saw some concerned partners claiming the game’s relationship mechanic was technically “cheating.” According to the survey, just 8% of those surveyed genuinely felt this way — but we’ll just have to see how things pan out once the game is actually in players’ hands.

GTA 6 releases on November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, and Xbox X|S.

You'll need to take the fight to him and Behemoth, and this is officially the endgame of the story, so you'll need to prepare for its biggest challenges.

Here's how to complete Chapter 8 of Final Fantasy Resonance, including all major objectives, boss encounters, and points of interest along the way.

Once you've returned to the airship, now is a good time to wrap up any side content you want to complete ahead of this chapter's final events. When you're ready to continue the main story, steer the airship in the direction of the giant crystal tower for a cutscene. As the airship approaches, Evan remarks that they can't get close to the top of the tower due to some kind of energy repelling them. Instead, they'll need to get as close as possible elsewhere within the tower. As Sakura and Rain are dropped off on an outer ledge of the tower, Sakura destroys a energy crystal barrier blocking a way inside. The rest of the group joins them and Raegen reminds them of what's at stake if the gate isn't closed soon. He says that in order to combat the gate's pull and its release of energy, he'll absorb that energy himself to at least displace it.

With their plan in motion, it's time to head inside. Save at the nearby Save Point and then go inside. After another brief cutscene, follow the path forward until you reach a fork. First go right to grab a Tablet Shard at the end of that route. Now go left and follow that route until you get to another fork. Run up the far-left route to branches into dead ends with both a Tablet Shard and a treasure coffer that contains a Pilebunker weapon (increases stagger power by 40% when using attacks of the target's elemental weakness) for Lid (seen above). Backtrack and take the right route now. Soon you'll see a narrower path that branches off to the north and leads down a ramp ahead. Take it to a hidden room that contains a Magic Pot (Lvl. 55 Pearly Pot) and a treasure coffer that contains an Apocalypse weapon (grants Protect for 3 turns upon staggering an enemy) for Rain. Backtrack to the main path and soon you'll get a cutscene. Fina again finds herself struggling to keep up, and Archwitch Fina tends to her. She surmises that she herself is drawing in energy from her younger self, and that if it continues, younger Fina will cease to exist. Despite this revelation, younger Fina says that what matters most to her is protecting her friends and helping them save the world. What happens after doesn't matter to her. Archwitch Fina looks on with empathy as her younger self runs off, and the scene ends. Continue going right and then briefly detour south for another treasure coffer (seen above). Open it to get 2 x Chef's Knife . Now head north and follow the path until you get to the next Save Point . Rest and save your progress, then use the teleport portal nearby to be taken to the next section and another cutscene. The group manages to catch up with Sol and Bahamut and they demand he stops. However, his warped conviction that all life mush perish holds, and he not only declares with pride that he'll be the one to do it, but that he'll show them how repugnant life truly is at the top of the tower.

In the meantime, he summons numerous monsters to hold them at bay, and the odds are definitely not in their favor. However, out of nowhere, multiple shots fly through and demolish most of the creatures for them. Both Alluvion and Lux come to meet them, much to the group's surprise.

Determined to help them stop Sol, they offer to help hold the line, and you'll then be pulled into a boss fight.

At the front of this pack is Dante, and he'll be flanked by two Specter enemies, whom you may have already encountered while running through the tower. Similar to other boss fights with minions, your first priority is to take them out first. They're weak to both Light and Ice magic, so make use of both to end them quickly.

Once only Dante is left, focus him down with both Light and Stone magic, his two weaknesses. His attacks are primarily physical ones that don't hit too hard at your current levels, so throw on Protega if you want while you work on staggering him. Once the mob is defeated, the following cutscene sees the group reunite with both Alluvion and Lux. Alluvion says that helping save the world from annihilation is part of her atonement, and Lux says she somewhat still finds the will to fight, despite having lost everything. With that, your group moves to press onward. Once you have control again, you'll see two paths marked by stairwells. Go up the left-side path first and follow it all the way to two treasure coffers. Open them to get 1 x Megalixir and a Laevateinn weapon (increases MP cost by 50% but increases damage by 100%) for Sakura.

Now backtrack and take the right-side stairs this time up to the path on that side. Follow it until you reach the next Save Point. Save your progress, then detour to the left for a treasure coffer nearby. Open it to get an Ancient Katana weapon for Lasswell. From there, keep heading left and through the exit ahead, which brings you to another ledge outside where another dark crystal barrier blocks the platform. Have Sakura destroy it and your airship will now be able to land at Crystal Tower - Middle Reach .

Tip: Now is a good time to replenish any valuable supplies before going forward, so take the opportunity to hop on your airship!

Now backtrack all the way to the previous Save Point and heal/save again before taking the north path. Soon you'll get a cutscene where the group catches up yet again to Sol and Behemoth. Sol and Rain argue about how humanity chooses to live, with Sol claiming that humans are selfish with only conflict as a means to live and progress. Rain rebuffs his words, saying that he would have never gotten this far if that were the case. Sol becomes exasperated and opts to have Behemoth put a stop to them. However, Lux and Alluvion step in to help. With that, get ready for a fierce battle.

The battle starts with Archwitch Fina saying that Behemoth is extremely resistant to all manner of attacks, be they physical or magic ones. This is a trait that ties directly into this fight's special mechanics, which involves scripted assistance from both Alluvion and Lux.

As the battle begins, your goal at this juncture is essentially to just survive while Alluvion and Lux prepare their attacks for Behemoth. However, in the meantime, while your attacks will only do 1 damage to its health, you'll still want to focus your efforts on its stagger meter, as that remains vulnerable. Behemoth is weak to both Light and Wind magic, so prioritize those elements for staggering. During this phase, also have Rain use Provoke to draw Behemoth's single-target attacks toward him, so that you don't have to exhaust MP and healing items on the entire group. Soon, Alluvion will use an attack that renders Behemoth vulnerable to magic attacks, so that's your cue to unleash your strongest Light and/or Wind attacks on it. Sometime later, Lux will attack Behemoth and that will make the beast vulnerable to physical attacks instead. So STOP attacking with straight magic attacks at that juncture and pivot to physical attacks (magic-imbued ones are fine, so Light/Wind accessories like Slyph's Tiara are great choices here). This flip-flop of magic and physical attacks will continue until both Alluvion and Lux attack at once, and this leaves Behemoth vulnerable to everything now. At that point, you can treat it like a normal fight and balance both types of attacks.

Be sure to watch out for Behemoth's strong magic attacks such as Flare (single-target), Thunderspark (single-target), Darkga (single-target), Burn to Ashes (party-wide), Chain Spark (party-wide), and Meteor (party-wide). Meanwhile, Stranglehold can inflict Paralysis on the target, which can spell trouble for your party if not mitigated or cleansed, so be mindful.

Once Behemoth is defeated, you'll get an emotional cutscene with both Alluvion and Lux, who both expended the last of the power from their armor. Nichol and Sakura tend to them, and the scene ends in a tragic farewell to the remaining members of the Sworn Six.

Raegen urges them to honor their sacrifice by pressing on, as Sol remains the biggest threat.

Once you have control again, double back down the stairs to save and heal up at the previous Save Point . Now press onward into the next area.

In the next section, you'll see platforms with what looks like impassable gaps. However, simply run forward and invisible paths will reveal themselves. If you feel comfortable contending with the random encounters (avg. Level 52) in this area, then feel free to explore all the possible paths for treasure coffers.

For instance, one on the far-right side (seen above) contains a Hastur Long Barrel weapon (Inflicts Deprotect on a random enemy at the start of battle) for Jake. Another coffer on the east of the room also has a Book of Eibon weapon for Nichol. Meanwhile, a coffer on the far-left side of the room has a Dragon Whisker weapon for Archwitch Fina.

To progress to the next area toward Sol, navigate the paths on the far-left side of the room until you reach the wide platform on the other side. Once there, run to the right until you get a cutscene.

An earthquake shakes the tower, catching the party off-guard. Sakura warns that it's an omen of things to come with the gate, so they need to hurry. As they do, Fina stumbles once more, her symptoms getting worse. Archwitch Fina stays behind with her and asks if she can hold up. Again, younger Fina assures that she can and that she's "content" with everything that's she's experienced up to this point.

However, as Archwitch Fina turns to go ahead, younger Fina collapses in sadness, revealing that she doesn't want to disappear. Archwitch Fina seemingly overhears her words from above, and the scene then ends.

Once you have control again, go up the next set of stairs and then all the way to the right to the exit. This brings you to another outdoor platform. Sakura will destroy the harmful crystal blocking it, and this opens the Upper Reach landing for your airship.

You may want to restock on some items after your encounter with Behemoth, so take the opportunity to do so. This section of the tower is also a great chance to level, if you feel like you're lagging a bit behind in that aspect.

Once you're ready to proceed, go up the next set of stairs to the Save Point ahead. Save, heal up if needed, and open the nearby treasure coffers for 1 x Magicite Cryst and a Faerie Bow weapon (grants Faith for 3 turns at the start of battle) for Fina.

WARNING: This is the point of no return in story progression. Make sure you're ready before stepping onto the white teleport portal.

Take the white teleport portal to your next destination. The following cutscene shows the group confront Sol once more, who seems surprised that you bested Behemoth. However, his resolve in bringing the world and all life on it to its knees remains unshaken, and he summons what looks a giant orb of dark energy, which he refers to as Chaotic Darkness . He calls it the "embodiment of the human mind and its desires", and it rises to the very peak of the tower.

However, to put a stop to it, you'll need to deal with Sol himself first. He morbidly welcomes the challenge, and the fight begins.

Sol will begin the fight by summoning Dark Bahamut as its minion. However, your goal here actually isn't to defeat it. Rather, it serves as an overpowered distraction, and you need to survive its Megaflare attack that comes in 3 turns. A countdown timer will begin, and the Dark Bahamut will cast Mighty Aura on itself, buffing its physical and magical attack power. Dispel it quickly to make its attacks more manageable in the meantime.

While it seems counterintuitive, be wary of casting buffs on your party . If you cast more than four different types of buffs across the group, Sol will respond with his Negation skill (every fourth action) that removes every buff you have. So choose wisely what you want to use ahead of Bahamut's Megaflare.

Once Bahamut expends its Megaflare attack, it will then vanish from the fight (for now), hence why you don't want to waste your turns on them. Focus all your offensive efforts on Sol, who is only weak to Dark magic, so Sakura and Archwitch Fina will shine here if you have them in your group. Otherwise, Visions who specialize in Dark magic can work as well. Sol's arsenal consists of almost all magic attacks, such as Blizzaga, Banishga, Aeroga, Flare, and Meteor. He'll also try to cripple your party at various junctures with debuffs like Deprotega and Deshellga while also occasionally buffing himself with those mitigations, so be sure to Dispel them.

Once Sol's health drops below 60%, he'll start incorporating his two biggest attacks. One is Ultima, which is a non-elemental magic attack that hits the entire party for massive damage. The other is Time Unwound, which gives Sol an extra move for two consecutive turns (unless he's staggered).

Once Sol is defeated here, you'll get another cutscene where the orb of Chaotic Darkness reveals a skeletal monstrosity, leaving the party almost frozen in fear and disbelief. For a moment, helplessness descends on the ground, and Archwitch Fina embraces Rain, saying, "this is the end, after all". However, Rain's resolve to save everyone in their world doesn't waver in the slightest.

With that, it's time to scale the remainder of the crystal tower to put an end to Sol's warped creation. You'll be transported onto a winding path that spirals up to the tower's peak. Along the way you may get pulled into random encounters with Metal Gigantuars (drop Remedies and you'll unlock the Priceless Experience trophy/achievement for defeating one).

Near the top of the spire you'll be safe from random encounters and there's a tunnel opening. Go inside and you'll find shop NPCs, a Moogle of Light, and a Save Point.

FINAL WARNING: Make the most of this rest stop and replenish any resources you need before going forward. There are NO other chances to rest or alter your party's setup once you reach the top, and this final section consists of multiple challenging bosses, so MAKE SURE YOU'RE READY BEFORE PROCEEDING.

As soon as your party reaches the top, they'll come face-to-face with the monstrosity that lies at the core of the Chaotic Darkness that Sol has summoned. With no other choice but to vanquish it to save the world from its wrath, they draw their weapons and the fight begins.

Tip: To contend with this boss's three different weaknesses (Wind, Stone, and Light), we highly recommend bringing Jake equipped with either Tidus or Clive and Sakura with the Onion Knight. Lid can help as a backup with Stone magic as well.

In this encounter, Chaotic Darkness consists of three main targets, and they must all be defeated one by one. They consist of the head (named Chaotic Darkness), a Left Hand, and a Right Hand. Each has its own stats, weaknesses, and movesets, meaning that each gets its own turn throughout the fight. This can make the start of the fight especially precarious, so start your party out with plenty of buffs before soldiering forward.

You want to focus down both Hands first, but in a specific order for a very specific reason.

Tip: Pay attention to which is Left and which is Right, as it's from the POV of the boss!

Start with the Left Hand , which is the one that doles out magic attacks such as Waterga, Firaga, Darkga, Chain Spark, Hell's Pillar, and Calamity. The hand is weak to Wind, so have your Wind users focus their efforts on this one. The reason you want to take this one out first is because it has the ability to resurrect the Right Hand.

Once the Left Hand is out of the equation, this will leave the boss unable to use its ultimate Ray of Apocalypse attack, as both Hands are required for it.

Now turn your focus to the Right Hand , which weak to Stone (or Earth), and primarily uses physical attacks such as Flatten (single-target), Rend (single-target), Rabid Claw (single-target; can inflict Confusion and/or Berserk), True Strike (single-target), Thwack (party-wide), Crushing Grasp (can inflict Paralysis), and Death Claw (drains 99% of target's HP and inflicts Paralysis).

Once both Hands are destroyed, focus your attacks on the body (Chaotic Darkness), which is weak to Light. Fina and Sakura are best for this section thanks to their Stagger-heavy skills, and the Warrior of Light is arguably the best Vision for Light damage.

Once the HP of the body falls below 60% it will gain a second move per turn, so beware. Its main attacks consist of Rib (single-target), Atomic Flare (single-target), Flare (single-target), Doom. Occasionally it will throw in devastating party-wide attacks such as Windstorm and Disaster, which can inflict a variety of status ailments (Ribbons are a lifesaver here).

Ensure your party stays topped off on health and MP (a trove of Ethers and Potions is a necessity for this section) throughout this encounter, and make the most of your staggers.

Once Chaotic Darkness is felled, you'll get a lengthy cutscene with the party as they initially celebrate their victory. However, something doesn't seem right and soon the party is dragged into pools of darkness beneath their feet, one by one. Just when it seems like all is lost, however, Rain manages to find his way to the others in the darkness, and they break free of it thanks to the prayers from loved ones around Lapis.

As they return to the peak of the tower, Chaotic Darkness seems to unravel and soon reveals its true form, an amalgamation of monsters that represent humanity's sins. Prepare yourself, as this is the next major step in the final conflict.

You're then throw headlong into the next battle.

This boss is comprised of several different mini bosses, each with its own stats, mechanics, and weaknesses. The initial cutscene shows your Visions come together to essentially "seal" three of the monsters within the glob, rendering them unable to fight (for now) while four others remain active.

Aside from the Keen of Fury which always unseals last, which of these mini-bosses start active reportedly depends on the Visions your entire roster has equipped (still unconfirmed which Vision seals which monster). During the fight, a new feature will unlock for your entire party roster called Last Resonance (located in the Skills menu). This is a special skill each character has that they can unleash at any time. However, the time to use it is when a monster's HP falls to 20-30% and it will react with a buff that boosts all its stats by 40% (indicated by a frowning face icon).

If you successfully use a character's Last Resonance skill in that window of opportunity, it will successfully inflict Death and defeat that monster. It will also immediately follow up with their respective Vision's Resonance attack, dealing even more damage to the remaining monsters. Once done, that character and their Vision will also be removed from the fight and replaced with a reserve party member (if there is one). As such, make sure that everyone in your roster has a Vision equipped for this stage .

Your goal here is to defeat each of the monsters at the right moment with your Last Resonances, down to the final ones which consist of The Keen of Fury and Chaotic Darkness itself. You want to destroy The Keen of Fury first, as if Chaotic Darkness falls below a certain percentage, it will absorb The Keen of Fury to replenish HP and buff itself. As your party will be dwindling by that point, make sure that everyone in your roster is well-equipped and self-reliant enough to stay alive through the end of this fight , otherwise you may find yourself with your hands tied and not enough staying power to fully defeat Chaotic Darkness.

Once the fight is over, you'll get another lengthy cutscene where Chaotic Darkness finally dissipates and the party rejoices as Raegen goes to take care of the gate in the sky. However, younger Fina sudden falls to her knees, her body threatening to fully fade away. Rain panics but Fina assures him that she has no regrets, as she was able to fight beside them to the end. With Sakura not sure what to do, Rain begs Archwitch Fina for help, which leaves her emotionally torn. Sir Raegen suddenly plummets back to the platform and says he's unable to close the gate because of one last obstacle. Sol hovers above them all, declaring that they won't interfere. A massive earthquake then shakes the land around them, and Sakura says the land is rising up towards the gate because there's no crystal to anchor it now. She laments that they're too late to stop it. However, Rain forbids them to give up, that they won't until the moment the land is truly gone. Archwitch Fina then claims that there is a way, and that is for her to go to the Earth Shrine to seal herself within a crystal. This time, however, she'll be the crystal itself rather than just sealed inside it. She also says that doing so will allow younger Fina to live on, as she won't require her energy anymore. Archwitch Fina bids them farewell and teleports to the Earth Shrine alone. She takes a moment to reminiscence about the past she spent exploring the land in spirit, particularly around Rain. She then undergoes the ritual to become a crystal, and the scene then pivots back to the crystal tower. The land stops shaking, leaving Sol in confusion while the group breathes relief. Younger Fina says she feels full of power now, and that she feels her "other me" watching over her.

Suddenly they realize the crystal tower is starting to collapse and they need to retreat back to the airship. As they flee, Fina uses her newfound power from her Archwitch self to clear debris in their path. Soon they make it back to the airship and make their escape. While pondering what comes next, they realize the land is still getting pulled in somehow. Sol's voice echoes in Rain's mind as his form appears on the deck of the airship, and he says that just as their light grows to overcome the darkness, the darkness will grow in turn to do the same. He asks if Rain wants to stop him and offers to settle things there and now, one on one.

Rain silently agrees and just as Lasswell asks him what's wrong, Rain says he's going to take care of it himself and leaps from the airship down to the remains of the crystal tower, where Sol is waiting.

The two finally go head-to-head to decide the world's fate.

This is somewhat of a scripted fight, but you still need to fight with the purpose of winning. This version of Sol is far weaker with only 13,500 HP but an abnormally high stagger gauge at 3,000. Your goal here isn't to stagger him into defeat, as you'll deplete his health much faster.

As expected, you're fighting solo as Rain here, so keep your own health and stats in mind. Sol is still weak to Dark magic, so if you have a Vision such as Shantotto, Sephiroth, or Cecil equipped to him, you can make things much easier with their attacks. However, Rain's fire-based arsenal can still work well enough. Once Rain's Limit Burst gauge fills quite quickly, use either of his Limit Bursts to end the fight.

With this final encounter, you'll then be treated to a lengthy sequence of cutscenes that concludes the story. No spoilers here, as you've more than earned this victory, so enjoy the ending!

Tip: After the story concludes, you'll gain access to the game's post-game content which consists of some new high-level content such as superbosses, Cave Masters, challenging dungeons, hidden Visions, the 12 Legendary Arms (a.k.a Weapons), The Champion League and the Grandshelt Colosseum (if you haven't taken a crack at that already).

There is no New Game Plus mode in Final Fantasy Resonance, so just go for that full completion!

articles.body:
Eleanor is a distinct NPC that you can encounter while playing Probably Stolen. She has a unique story where you can have direct impacts on what happens to her. If you're willing to help her out, she does provide you with a worthwhile reward. In this guide, we're going to cover everything you need to know about completing Eleanor's questline while playing Probably Stolen.

How to Complete Eleanor's Questline in Probably Stolen

Eleanor will appear to you within the first two or three weeks of opening your shop. She tells you that she's been stranded in the Lower Levels because her mother's been taken to jail. She's not too sure about the reason, but wants to try to purchase basic supplies from you when she meets you, and wants to buy food so she can survive. You can sell any type of food to her, and she'll be on her way.

After this, she'll appear again within the next few days. Eleanor explains that things are getting worse, and she's going to remain here in the Lower Levels for much longer than she planned, as her mother is still in jail. Now, she's going to ask to buy Household Supplies from you so she can survive. You can provide any type of Household item to her, and she'll be on her way.

The third time that Eleanor appears, she's running out of money. She doesn't have many other options available to her, and wants to sell you the few items she has so he can continue to buy supplies and stay alive. She's going to sell you several luxury items, which you can turn around and sell to others in the Lower Levels for a reasonable price.

Now, before you see Eleanor again, an individual is going to appear as "Eleanor's Uncle," with a supply package for Eleanor. He's going to give it to you for free and have you ask no further questions. However, if you hover over the item, it's labeled with the five-finger discount, and it's noted as stolen. If you take it, the man leaves it with you.

You have the option to give this crate to Eleanor, or keep it. If you give it to Eleanor, she gets arrested immediately and goes into jail with her mother. However, if you hold onto the item and do not give it to Eleanor, her story continues. Eventually, the Care Package crate loses its stolen rating, and you can open it up or sell it to others for a great price. I do recommend selling it.

A few days later, Eleanor tells you she's made a discovery that she's certain that someone framed her mother. She's not sure who, or why they did it. However, despite not having access to her money, she's going to try to earn it. Her new roommate in the Lower Levels has shown her how to scavenge in the Dumping Area for good items, and brings you a random supply of things she's found out in this area. She's looking to get at least 850 credits to save her mother. You don't have to get her to this amount right away. You can take a few days, slowly purchasing items she brings until she has enough to buy a Private Investigator.

When she reaches her amount, a few days pass, and Eleanor comes to you to share that her mother was working on genetic research for Nutrifruit, and that she had discovered a way to bring seeds for the fruit, allowing others to farm these without having the Corporations involved. She says she needs a few days to process this information, and departs.

Before you see her again, a Black Market Thug appears and warns you that if Eleanor doesn't give the genetic research back that she got about her mother, her mother is going to die. However, if she does give it back (and you convince her to do it), you'll get 300 credits for it.

Next, Eleanor appears to tell you she got the same threat. If she announces the truth about the research, her mother is going to die. But if she gives up the research, the two of them live, and they can return to their old life. You'll have the option to convince Eleanor of the choice that she wants to make.

By encouraging Eleanor to come forward about the genetic research, her mother is killed. Still, the Nutrifruit discovery helps a lot more people than it hurts, and provides a better life for others. Eleanor will also share that, with her mother dead, she's going to fight against the Corporations and join the Revolution, asking for a weapon before she leaves your vendor.

If you tell her to give the genetic research up, her mother lives. But the research doesn't come to light, and others don't benefit from this discovery.

Both options give the same item, as well: a SYNC Self-Refilling Neuroactive Perfume. It gives you a 15% profit boost with one customer you use it with. The bottle has five uses and refills a use every three days.

articles.title: Resident Evil Lands on Digital After Monstrous Box Office Run
articles.body:
Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil is now available to rent or purchase digitally from services like Prime Video . The move to digital comes just over 45 days after the movie’s release in theaters, where the Capcom adaptation had quite the run.

After a monstrous opening weekend , Resident Evil climbed to the top of the list of highest-grossing video game movies . The zombie flick just crossed over $400 million at the global box office, and if it manages to pick up another $30 million, has a chance of breaking into the top 10 highest-grossing horror movies of all time .

Resident Evil Lands on Digital After Crushing Box Office Expectations

Resident Evil is now available to purchase digitally for $24.99 . The film is also up for preorder on DVD, Blu-ray, and 4K , though the DVD release still doesn’t have a release date.

The path to Resident Evil’s box office glory hasn’t exactly been easy. Cregger himself recently spoke out about the disappointment he’s felt about the conversation centering entirely on the movie's relationship to the Capcom games.

Before the movie was even released, early conversations were driven around what exactly Cregger would be adapting, and of course fans were demanding a direct adaptation of popular RE characters like Leon Kennedy. In Cregger’s words , early fan reactions made him feel like he was doing “an apology tour."

Nonetheless, Cregger stood by his decision to adapt the “feeling of playing Resident Evil,” rather than any of the specific games, and in so doing, we believe captured a lot of what makes the games great .

We’re also of the opinion that it’s a great movie for movie’s sake, offering something to both dedicated fans of the games as well as newcomers just looking for some zombie action. In his review for IGN , Tom Jorgensen makes a direct address to those coming from the Capcom world: “Whatever your idea of what a good Resident Evil movie should be, I have to recommend to the skeptical to put that to one side and lock in for what Zach Cregger delivers.”

And what exactly does Cregger deliver? In Jorgensen's words, "a jet-fueled horror experience that has room for lots of tension, some great laughs, and a strong central performance from Austin Abrams."

Nonetheless, the movie’s release did spur increased interest in the gaming franchise, with Resident Evil 2 Remake sales on PS5 up more than 50% the week the movie dropped in theaters. This wider audience interest is just one piece of a particularly successful year for Capcom, which also saw the acclaimed releases of Resident Evil Requiem and, more recently, Onimusha: Way of the Sword .

Studios are naturally eyeing more video game adaptation opportunities, with one producer from Resident Evil already turning his attention to a Silent Hill movie . Cregger himself said early on that this would be the end of his involvement in the Resident Evil franchise, but more recently stated he'd be willing to "have a hand" in future sequels.

In the meantime, Cregger will be following in the footsteps of Kane Parsons' Backrooms by producing an adaptation of an internet horror legend, Siren Head .

articles.title: Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross Have Provided the Score to David Fincher's The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
articles.summary: Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross Have Provided the Score to David Fincher's The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth
articles.body:
Nine Inch Nails bandmates and award-winning film composers Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross are once again partnering up to provide the score for David Fincher's new film, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. This marks the sixth collaboration between the musical pair and the director.

Reznor and Ross' involvement was revealed when Netflix debuted the official poster for the film on its social media accounts earlier today, and you can seem them listed in the credits at the bottom of the image below (if you squint hard enough).

GET TICKETS NOW. THE FURTHER MIS-ADVENTURES OF CLIFF BOOTH. ONLY IN IMAX NOVEMBER 25. — Netflix (@netflix) November 2, 2026

GET TICKETS NOW. THE FURTHER MIS-ADVENTURES OF CLIFF BOOTH. ONLY IN IMAX NOVEMBER 25.

Reznor and Ross previously featured on the soundtracks to Fincher-directed films including The Social Network, Gone Girl, and Mank, with the former receiving the Academy Award for Best Original Score in 2011. More recently the pair won the Golden Globe Award for the Best Original Score for Challengers in 2025, and earned a Grammy nomination earlier this year for one of its tracks from the Tron: Ares soundtrack (credited as Nine Inch Nails).

The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is a sequel to Quentin Tarantino's Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, written by Tarantino and featuring Brad Pitt in a reprisal of his stuntman role, but directed by Fincher. In a recent interview with Empire Magazine, Fincher revealed that Tarantino's original draft "was essentially two movies" and that he had to cut 60 pages from the screenplay in order to get the film down to a runtime of around two hours and 20 minutes.

The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is set to open in IMAX theaters globally on November 25, before it launches on Netflix on December 23. Alongside Brad Pitt, the film is also set to star Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul Mateen II, and Peter Weller. Tarantino is set to release a novelization of the film on December 8, which will serve as a literary follow-up to 2021's Once Upon a Time in Hollywood: A Novel.

articles.title: LEGO Godzilla Announced, Releases on Black Friday
articles.summary: LEGO has announced it's releasing a huge new LEGO Godzilla set on November 27, which is also Black Friday 2026.
articles.body:
Each year, LEGO releases a major new set on Black Friday . The block-building company has just announced this year’s set: It’s LEGO Godzilla, a 5,363-piece build that will cost $449.99 ( see it at LEGO ).

This gray-and-blue beast from the Monsterverse stands over 27.5 inches tall and can be posed in a number of different ways. If you buy it between November 27 - 30 while supplies last, you’ll also get a LEGO Godzilla Logo & Footprint set for free as a Gift With Purchase.

Fitting with the subject, this is a large, imposing set, with the city-destroying monster standing over two feet tall. The beast’s skin is made up of overlapping gray LEGO bricks, some smooth, and some with “ greebling ” to create a scaly effect. His dorsal fins are jagged and detailed, made of blocks with varying shades of blue. The overall effect makes it look organic and fiery – it’s very cool.

When you have it built, you can adjust the position of Godzilla’s tail to the left or right. You can also move its head, arms, wrists, and fingers. It comes with a tongue you can put in his mouth, or a blue Heat Ray to add a more dynamic, destructive vibe to the King of Monsters.

LEGO Godzilla springs from the LEGO Ideas line, where fans and amateur builders can create their own designs and submit them for consideration for official release. The original designer of the LEGO Ideas submission for Godzilla is fan designer Matthew Esposito, or MattE720 . Once the set received 10,000 votes, LEGO agreed to release the set and had professional designers work with Esposito on the final design for release.

LEGO Godzilla will be available exclusively at the LEGO Store starting at 12:01 a.m. on November 27. Major sets like this tend to sell out very quickly, so if you want it, I’d recommend staying up and buying it right when the listing goes live.

If you buy it early enough, you’ll also get LEGO Godzilla Logo & Footprint as a free Gift With Purchase. This is a 359-piece set that accompanies the main set and is meant to be displayed near it. It features a blue Godzilla logo standing over a giant reptilian footprint.

For more, check out our list of every upcoming LEGO set announced to date.

articles.title: The Ultra-Slim Baseus Blade 20,000mAh Power Bank With 100W Output Drops to $39 for Black Friday
articles.summary: This 0.7" thin power bank boasts high capacity and output for handheld gaming PCs and laptops.
articles.body:
Looking for a high-capacity, high-output power bank with an ultra-slim footprint? Ahead of Black Friday, Amazon has dropped the price of the Baseus Blade 20,000mAh 100W power bank to just $39.49 shipped after you apply coupon code " Z6J1ANOV ". You do NOT have to be an Amazon Prime member. Unlike most high-capacity power banks that are shaped like a chunky bar, the Baseus Blade is slimmer. It's powerful enough to charge any gaming handheld PC at its fastest rate. This is consistently one of the most popular power banks on IGN whenever I post a deal for it (which isn't often).

Baseus Blade 20,000mAh 100W Slim Power Bank for $39.49

Baseus Blade 20,000mAh 100W Slim Power Bank

The Baseus Blade measures only 0.7 inches thick. Most high-capacity power banks are well over 1" in thickness. The Blade achieves this slim depth by going with a wider body design. The form factor allows it to fit perfectly in a laptop bag or backpack sleeve. It still weighs in at about one pound which is comparable to other power banks, so no give or take there.

The wide body allows it to squeeze in four ports: two USB Type-C ports each with 100W of Power Delivery and two USB Type-A ports each with 30W output. Note that the maximum charging output is 100W. That means although all three ports add up to a total of 160W, only a maximum of 100W will be delivered across all three ports if they are used simultaneously.

The 20,000mAh capacity can fully recharge your gaming handhelds

This Baseus Blade boasts a generous 20,000mAh, or 74Whr battery capacity. If you factor in 80% power efficiency, here are the approximate number of times you can fully recharge each gaming handheld or iPhone model:

Nintendo Switch 2 (18Whr) about 3.3 times

Steam Deck (40-50Whr) about 1.2-1.5 times

Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max (20Whr) about 3 times

The 100W output can fast charge nearly all phones and gaming handhelds

The Baseus Blade has USB Type-C ports that provides up to 100W of power output but it will automatically throttle down to whatever maximum rate the plugged-in device accepts. The Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 can only accept a maximum of 18W-30W of power output. The Steam Deck can accept up to 45W. The Legion Go S accepts up to 55W. The Xbox ROG Ally X can actually accept charging rates of up to 100W.

This power bank can be brought onto airplanes

You don't need to worry about being stopped at airports. The 20,000mAh 74Whr capacity is well below TSA's 27,000mAh/100Whr carry-on limit, so you are safely in the clear.
